text.p: Finnish plastic pipes, white goods and furniture maker Asko Oy in its 1996 annual report raised earnings expectations for 1997 to "better than in 1996" from "at least the same level as in 1996" announced a month ago.
Writing in the annual report, managing director Jarmo Rytilahti said targets had been set with the aim that "in 1997, the group will achieve a better result than in 1996."
Asko's strategic goal is to reach an equity to assets ratio of 40 percent by the end of 1998, he said. In 1996, Asko's equity ratio rose 4.9 percentage points to 32.9 percent.

"The group's board has decided on a dividend policy according to which about one quarter of group earnings after taxes will be distributed as dividends as long as the equity to assets ratio is below 40 percent," Rytilahti said.
In 1996, EPS was 36.70 markka and the dividend 10.00 markka.
Investments in new products and production capacity lay in store for Asko's biggest business area, plastics pipes maker Uponor, Rytilahti said, adding these were aimed at securing organic growth.
"Company acquisitions are also an essential part of the growth strategy," he added, but did not elaborate.

The chosen investment strategy combined with the target to raise the equity ratio meant that in the future, too, Asko would "determinedly realise fixed assets without excluding giving up certain branches," Rytilahti said, again without elaborating. --Helsinki newsroom +358-9-680 50 245, e-mail news@reuters.fi
